overclaims: Neither source identifies the VC-funded subsidy mechanism or measures the additional lab revenue it supposedly causes.
checks.note: The excerpt, proposition, condition, axis, outcome and citations all check out. The Vercel and Ramp points in the rationale are supported. The one problem is the word 'supposedly' in the rationale, which is loaded and signals doubt about the speaker. It should be neutral, for example 'the additional lab revenue the claim attributes to it'.

The excerpt and proposition are faithful, including 'vast majority' and the exclusion of unprofitable AI startups. The rationale matches e7 (adoption rates within sectors) and e8 (a sample that skews toward tech, 70% software or fintech). The limitations cover the spending-weighted reading. The e7 and e8 excerpts, publishers, dates and relations are correct.

The criteria show the 'someone else will buy the compute' set-up, so 'No they won't' has its context. The rationale correctly treats the Microsoft campus in e2 as adjacent and announced in March 2026, before the post. It also correctly says that no qualifying replacement purchase by Oct 28 cannot support an open-horizon forecast. The open horizon and unresolved outcome match the reviews. Citations are correct.

The proposition keeps the full dependency chain, 'many of whom', 'on the low end', 2027 and 'over $200B'. The point about the Azure ambiguity ($174B vs $224B) and the point that available summaries repeat Zitron are both supported by the contract and packet. The Broadcom 8-K is described accurately as covering one arrangement. The e1 and e2 excerpts, dates and relations are correct.
